en: The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of exactly 7,641 islands, which are divided into three main island groups.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Mayon Volcano is the most active volcano in the Philippines, having recorded over 50 eruptions in the past 400 years.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest in the Philippines, extending about 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering approximately 14,649 square kilometers.
Baguio City is one of the wettest places in the Philippines, receiving an average annual rainfall of over 4,000 millimeters.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 96,828 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology monitors exactly 24 active volcanoes and 36 inactive volcanoes across the country.
The Philippine archipelago spans from 4 degrees to 21 degrees North latitude and from 116 degrees to 127 degrees East longitude.
